plugins.audit_text:
[`xtc_plugin.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-plugin-xtc/src/lib/xtc_plugin.rs):2001–2146 validates initialized rate/geometry, adopts prepared filters, freezes finite support at drain and reports FFT latency. Crosstalk cancellation is ill-conditioned at some frequencies/positions; gain limits and regularization are part of correctness, not just tonal preferences.

`xtc_validation.rs`, `stream_clock.rs`, `aligned_bypass.rs`, finite/autogain tests and reference fixtures are useful. The saturation quality test measures a settled sine peak; extend first-frame gain, head displacement, room mismatch and independent acoustic transfer matrices. Classical frequency-dependent regularization, robustness regions and measured head tracking are priorities. ML can estimate position or personalize transfer functions off the critical path; constrain the inverse filter's gain and retain measured validation.

[`delay_plugin.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-plugin-delay/src/lib/delay_plugin.rs):972–1125 resets delay/LFO/crossfade histories and drains bounded nonrecursive support. For feedback/recursive routes, native drain can report complete rather than synthesize an unbounded tail. That may be an intentional host contract, but a renderer must not assume all audible repeats are automatically emitted at EOF.

`audit_accuracy.rs`, `tail_length.rs`, `finite_stream.rs`, property and realtime parameter tests provide good foundations. Add end-to-end offline render tests with an explicit tail-duration/energy policy, feedback near its limit, delay changes and tempo discontinuities. Classical fractional delay, click-free dual taps and tape-style pitch modulation should be separate, tested modes. ML is unnecessary for the basic delay.

host_analyzers_and_adapters.audit_text:
**Spectrum analyzer.** [`analyzer_spectrum.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-host/src/analyzer_spectrum.rs):425–545 enforces initialization/rate, retains a recent-sample ring and computes channel power without cancellation from summing opposite-phase channels. It analyzes the most recent window after a block; a block spanning multiple FFT windows can omit intermediate windows. That is acceptable for a display only if specified, but unsuitable for guaranteed transient/peak capture. Extend calibrated bin-centered/off-bin tones, DC/Nyquist, impulses, channel anti-phase and arbitrary callback sizes. Offer explicit amplitude/PSD normalization and max-hold semantics. No ML is needed for a calibrated spectrum.

**Loudness monitor.** [`analyzer_loudness_monitor.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-host/src/analyzer_loudness_monitor.rs):2029–2089 preserves transparent audio, validates shape/rate and finalizes true-peak state at drain. This is a stronger EOF contract than simply stopping the meter. Extend independent conformance vectors, short clips, gating discontinuities, surround channel weights, disabled/re-enabled state and final publication under cache contention. Distinguish LUFS from psychoacoustic loudness/SPL. ML quality scores may be supplementary, never a substitute for calibrated measurement.

**AutoGain.** [`auto_gain.rs`](crates/sotf-plugins/crates/sotf-host/src/auto_gain.rs):281–395 uses sample-clocked gain trajectories and a settled fast path. Its integration into each effect must measure the intended pre/post stages and handle silence without runaway gain or level jumps. Existing per-plugin clock/heap tests are a major strength. Extend sparse transients, prolonged silence then signal, AB switching and peak-constrained gain recovery. Classical loudness/peak-constrained matching suffices; no learned gain controller is needed by default.

**External plugin factory route.** The `external`/`external_plugin` entry delegates to native formats and may use isolated workers. It inherits the scheduling, latency, parameter, state and sandbox boundaries discussed above, rather than one fixed DSP algorithm. Test process death, stale sequence, missed deadline, malformed state, latency change, instrument MIDI and output-channel changes against real AU/VST3/CLAP fixtures. Compare native and isolated audio after declared pipeline latency; fallback audio must remain distinguishable from successfully processed output. ML is not a substitute for process containment or ABI validation.

**Adapters/support crates.** `plugins-bridge`, `plugins-ffi`, `plugins-nih`, `plugins-gpui`, `plugins-spatial`, `plugins-denoiser` and `plugins-inference` are not seven more standalone DSP effects. They carry ABI, native-host, UI, spatial-data and inference contracts. A plugin passing its own crate tests does not prove its AU/VST3/CLAP/FFI form has correct parameter units, sample offsets, channel negotiation, latency change notification or tail handling. Add cross-wrapper audio equivalence and lifecycle suites, and run native-feature builds on their supported platforms. Inference already uses generation-tagged bounded handoff; retain that architecture and explicitly constrain allocation/destruction and model shutdown.
